description: The authors propose a graphic reinterpretation of the original CoI framework in which learner presence replaces educational experience at the center of the overlapping teaching, social, and cognitive presences.
title: Learner-centered reinterpretation of the CoI framework placing learner presence at the intersection of the three presences

description: The learner-centered paradigm replaces a time-fixed, group-based, sorting-oriented school system with one that holds attainment constant and lets pace and path vary to fit each learner.
title: Learner-Centered Paradigm of Education

description: The guide adopts Carl Rogers' view that \"we cannot teach a person anything directly; we can only facilitate his or her learning\" as its organising framework for adult language teaching.
title: Learner-centred facilitation of adult language learning

description: The paper envisions Learner Positioning Systems, analogous to a geographic GPS, that help learners position themselves in their learning.
title: Learner Positioning System (LPS): a GPS-like system positioning each learner with a learner profile, learning map, and resource bank

description: The paper's organizing framework is that no average learner exists: each learner has a distinctive profile of strengths and challenges, so instruction must be designed for variability rather than the middle.
title: Learner variability and jagged profiles as the foundation for personalized learning

description: The survey defines \"learner variability\" as a construct covering the abilities students have and the challenges they bring to learning.
title: Learner variability as a multidimensional construct spanning cognitive, social, emotional, and background factors

description: The article advances the account that children's learning-related behaviors, specifically task orientation, are a mechanism through which executive function relates to mathematics achievement.
title: Learning-related behaviors as a mechanism linking executive function to mathematics achievement

description: The article names and describes 'learning-centered learning,' a 21st-century construct that shifts educators' mindset from controlling teaching toward the learner and the learning process.
title: Learning-centered learning: a construct resting on five philosophical learning assumptions

description: The guide grounds its activities in the learning cycle, a sequence science educators have identified as \"an effective means for learning concepts and processes of science\" that is \"also...
title: Learning cycle instructional model: exploration, concept introduction, concept application

description: Learning engineering, as described in this report, applies engineering problem-solving processes to problems of educational practice: Uncapher described 'the synergy around design thinking and science of learning' as...
title: Learning engineering: educators take research and turn it into classroom solutions using engineering problem-solving processes

description: The article organizes its review around aspects of the learning environment that it identifies as most closely tied to early academic success.
title: Learning-environment aspects framework for early academic competence

description: The study uses mathematical learning progressions as the standard against which teachers' content adaptations to middle school math curricula are judged.
title: Mathematical learning progressions as a lens for evaluating teachers' curriculum adaptations

description: The article grounds the WEC's learning readiness construct in self-regulated learning theory, which it defines as \"the ability to regulate cognition, behaviours, and emotions to achieve academic goals\".
title: Learning readiness as an operationalization of self-regulated learning (SRL)

description: The article discusses learning styles theory as its theoretical framework for examining how students are classified by preferences for taking in, processing, and demonstrating information in education.
title: Learning styles theory as a theoretical framework for K-12 assessment and instruction

description: The article grounds its interdisciplinary course schedule in multiple learning theories that focus on exploratory learning environments.
title: Learning theories frame interdisciplinary discovery in the studio

description: The article frames a function as an encoding {F, x} relating a control parameter to a dependent value, and the Legendre transform as a second encoding {G, s} of the same information, where s is the derivative dF/dx.
title: The Legendre transform as an alternative encoding of the information in a function, forming a self-inverse conjugate pair

title: Leitner Queue Network

description: The report models communication between a student and a machine as occurring at three levels of discourse.
title: Levels of discourse taxonomy for student/computer interaction (L0, L1, L2)
